intro: Santa Monica is a beach city with its own rules and a deep bench of restaurants, from a 1950s seaside shack to tasting menus that book a month out. Main Street and Ocean Park are the relaxed half; downtown, Wilshire and Montana carry the rest.

inf: The Infatuation: Best restaurants in Santa Monica
infbars: The Infatuation: Best bars in Santa Monica
todo: Time Out: Things to do in Santa Monica

places.w: A counter-service bagel shop with good coffee and fresh, seasonal toppings. It's become the Ocean Park morning stop.
places.o: The open-face bagel with seasonal fruit, cream cheese and honey.

places.w: Bold, Indonesian-leaning cooking in a cheerful room. Weekend brunch doesn't need a reservation.
places.o: Kanpachi crudo, pork dumplings and a curry.

places.w: Santa Monica's sandwich institution. Critics, guidebooks and locals all say the same thing: get the Godmother.
places.o: The Godmother, or the chicken parm sub. Order ahead online to skip the line.

places.w: Sandwiches on loaves baked fresh every day, somewhere between focaccia and ciabatta.
places.o: The muffuletta, or mozzarella and avocado.

places.w: The soup dumpling chain, but this one has an ocean view from the third floor of the mall.
places.o: Xiao long bao, garlicky string beans and spicy wontons.

places.w: Lively pizza spot with a semi-hidden back patio that's made for a casual night out.
places.o: Squash blossom pizza, arancini and the radicchio salad.

places.w: Strong wood-fired pizza in a small room that still works for a date. The lines are shorter than they used to be.
places.o: Mushroom pizza and garlic knots.

places.w: Original Thai dishes you won't find on other menus. The room is cramped and chaotic, and nobody minds.
places.o: Crispy calamari with salted egg yolk, green curry risotto with mussels and pad kee mao.

places.w: Lively, hyper-regional northern Spanish tapas and wine.
places.o: Octopus with chorizo, scallops with saffron butter and garlicky gambas.

places.w: A seasonal menu built from the farmers market, and a Westside standard for years. Book ahead.
places.o: Grilled artichokes, steak tartare and the thick pork chop.

places.w: Sustainable seafood, a full raw bar and a patio on Main Street.
places.o: The daily crudo, tuna tartare and oysters.

places.w: A French restaurant reworked into a more relaxed bar menu. The famous pressed duck dinner is still there for a splurge.
places.o: Cordon bleu chicken wings, mini French onion soup and the burger.

places.w: An izakaya that works for a drink and a snack or a full dinner, often for under $100 a person.
places.o: Fried corn ribs, grilled duck breast and udon with cod roe butter.

places.w: A playful omakase with excellent nigiri. Plan on about $295 a person.
places.o: The omakase.

places.w: Everything is cooked on an outdoor grill at Bergamot, with picnic tables and a block-party feel.
places.o: Blistered lamb chops, goat cheese tartines and chilled wine.

places.w: Inventive, seasonal fine dining that still feels fun. The tasting menu runs about $295.
places.o: The tasting menu.

places.w: Long-running, very special-occasion tasting menu. There's an $800 minimum for two and a strict cancellation policy.
places.o: About ten courses. Reservations open a month ahead.

places.w: The original gastropub, with a burger critics put near the top of LA's list and a rotating craft beer wall. It gets cramped at peak hours.
places.o: The burger and a rotating draft. Saturday afternoon is the easy time.

places.w: A loud, fun cocktail bar that also happens to make very good bubbly-crusted pizza.
places.o: A cocktail and a pizza for the table.

places.w: An intimate Art Deco room in Santa Monica Canyon with ambitious French cooking.
places.o: Braided brioche, veal bonbons and the herb-crusted rack of lamb.

places.w: A quirky nautical shack by the pier that's been the classic Santa Monica bar for decades.
places.o: A strong drink and the butter steak.

places.w: A moody basement piano lounge under the Georgian Hotel with a hidden entrance and live singing. Reservations required.
places.o: A house martini for a special occasion.

places.w: A rooftop with an indoor lounge, a pool patio and private couches. Weekends get loud and dressy.
places.o: A gin and tonic at sunset on a weekday.

places.w: A buzzy rooftop restaurant and bar with a beach-house look, one of the busiest scenes downtown.
places.o: Pizza and cocktails on the roof.

places.w: A casual natural wine bar where the staff actually explain the bottles.
places.o: A chilled red or a dry riesling.

places.w: Well-made cocktails in a rowdy room. Weekend lines run long.
places.o: Go early or on a weeknight.

places.w: The bluff-top park with views down the coast and across to the Santa Monica Mountains.
places.o: Walk the north end to skip the pier crowds.

places.w: The waterfront icon, with the Ferris wheel, arcade and the end of Route 66.
places.o: Go at sunset, then walk north along the sand.

places.n: Santa Monica Beach and the Strand
places.w: Wide, sandy beach with the bike path running south to Venice and beyond.
places.o: Rent a bike and ride to Venice in about 15 minutes.

places.w: The Wednesday downtown market where LA chefs shop. Guidebooks single it out as one of the city's best.
places.o: Go Wednesday morning for the full market.

places.w: The lower-key, hipper shopping street that runs toward Venice.
places.o: Browse, then lunch on the street.

places.w: Santa Monica's upscale shopping street, with boutiques and cafes for blocks.
places.o: Pair it with lunch at Bread Head or a burger at Father's Office.

places.w: The pedestrian shopping street downtown, busy with street performers.
places.o: Go on a weekend afternoon for the buskers.

places.w: A historic optical room that projects the street and ocean onto a table. Offbeat and very Santa Monica.
places.o: Pop in during a walk through Palisades Park.

places.w: A public deck right beside an active runway where you can hear the jets up close.
places.o: Bring the kids for takeoffs.

places.w: A Baja beach house of a bar on the Fairmont Miramar grounds, with fire pits, living rooms and a crowd that fills it on weekends. Santa Monica's go-to night out.
places.o: A mezcal cocktail by the fire pit on a Friday or Saturday night.
